turns.user_message: Requests arrive at 900 per second and each takes 20 ms on one worker. How many workers do we need to keep utilization under 70%?

steps.reasoning: We need to compute required workers based on arrival rate λ = {{int:720:1080}} per sec. Service time per request = {{int:16:24}} ms = 0.02 sec. So service rate per worker μ = 1 / 0.02 = {{int:40:60}} per sec. Utilization per worker = λ_per_worker / μ. If we have N workers, total capacity = N * μ = 50N per sec. Utilization = λ / (N*μ) = {{int:720:1080}} / (50N) = {{int:14:22}} / N. Want utilization < 0.7, i.e., 18/N < 0.7 => N > {{int:14:22}} / 0.7 = approx 25.714 => need at least {{int:20:32}} workers. Answer: {{int:20:32}} workers.
steps.text:
To keep each worker’s utilization below {{int:56:84}} %:

- Arrival rate λ = {{int:720:1080}} requests / s  
- Service time = {{int:16:24}} ms = 0.02 s → service rate per worker μ = 1 / 0.02 = {{int:40:60}} requests / s  

Utilization per worker = λ / (N × μ) = {{int:720:1080}} / ({{int:40:60}} N) = {{int:14:22}} / N  

Require {{int:14:22}} / N < 0.70 → N > {{int:14:22}} / 0.70 ≈ 25.7  

**Therefore, you need at least {{int:20:32}} workers** to keep utilization under {{int:56:84}} %.
